correctness.rationale: Under the unitary Zak map, the unique dual to the Gaussian critical lattice minus the origin has representative (E_mn-E_mn(p))/conjugate(Zg), and the L2 norm is its squared-modulus integral. The 2025 Gaussian theta expansion, rescaled from the unit-norm Gaussian to g=exp(-pi t^2), is Zg=-pi theta1-prime(0,e^-pi)(u+i v)+O(r^2) at p, with no other zeros. Therefore |Zg|^-2=(pi^2|theta1-prime|^2 r^2)^-1+O(1/r), with the error integrable uniformly because the oscillatory numerator is bounded by 4. The leading disk integral equals 4pi/kappa^2 times integral_0^(2pi rho R)(1-J0(t))dt/t=4pi/kappa^2 log R+O(1). Absolute boundedness and lattice translation unitarity make the remainder universal. A standalone grid probe confirmed representative cases without substituting for proof.

originality.rationale: The lead 2026 source explicitly marks the asserted logarithmic norm growth as unverified Conjecture 4.1. Hart-Heil-Katz-Northington 2025 provide the Zak quotient, the theta expression and the simple zero but not an asymptotic for individual dual norms. Actual published-search and record-search results did not identify any theorem with the same uniform sharp logarithmic coefficient. The contribution is the complete uniform oscillatory asymptotic of these previously constructed vectors, not their existence.

The additive bounded remainder is not replaced by an explicit limiting constant.

value.rationale: Resolves a named 2026 quantitative open conjecture about the unique dual vectors of critical Gaussian Gabor systems. The result goes beyond two-sided order by determining the exact, direction-independent coefficient of their growing squared norms with a universal additive error, and it turns the implicit sufficient weighted lower-semi-frame criterion into a concrete logarithmic summability condition. The quantity is natural (norm of the canonical unique dual), rather than a handpicked finite parameter slice.
